preview_text: Erling Haaland scored four goals in Norway's first two group games against Iraq and Senegal before being rested as Norway fielded a heavily rotated side in a 4-1 loss to France in their final group match.

Martin Odegaard recorded two assists in the group stage as Norway's primary creator, while Marcus Pedersen opened the scoring against Senegal in Round 2. Norway scored ten goals across three group games, averaging 3.33 per match.

Norway advanced from Group I in second place behind France with six points. Their group stage produced 15 goals combined, the most of any team's group at the tournament, including a 3-2 win over Senegal in Round 2.

Erling Haaland anchors the slate as the highest-priced attacking option with four goals in his first two group games. Martin Odegaard offers a value pivot in the midfield with playmaking volume behind him.

Ivory Coast advanced from Group E in second place with two clean sheets in three group games, conceding only twice across the entire group stage. Their lone defeat came in stoppage time against Germany.

Yan Diomande has been Ivory Coast's most creative attacking outlet from midfield, while Amad Diallo and Nicolas Pepe served as the primary corner kick takers. Pepe led the team with two goals in the group stage.

Ivory Coast closed the group stage with a 2-0 win over Curaçao, their second clean sheet of the tournament. They opened the scoring in all three group matches, a feat achieved by only one other African nation in World Cup history.
Nicolas Pepe leads Ivory Coast in DFS value as the group stage top scorer, while Yan Diomande and Amad Diallo provide corner kick exposure and creative output from wide areas.

France swept Group I with wins over Senegal, Iraq, and Norway, scoring ten goals while conceding only twice. Ousmane Dembele scored a hat-trick in the 4-1 win over a heavily rotated Norway side in the final group game.

Kylian Mbappe scored in all three group games and leads France in attacking output, while Michael Olise served as corner kick taker. William Saliba was rested in the final group game with a minor back issue but is expected to start.

France became the first team since 1998 to win all three group games, scoring three or more goals in four consecutive matches dating back to their final group game. They have conceded just twice in three matches.
Kylian Mbappe is the top overall DFS asset on the slate with goals in every group game, while Ousmane Dembele offers a high-ceiling pivot off his hat-trick performance against Norway.

Sweden advanced as one of the best third-placed teams after a turbulent group stage that included a 5-1 win over Tunisia, a 5-1 loss to Netherlands, and a 1-1 draw with Japan in their final group match.

Anthony Elanga scored a long-range equalizer against Japan in the 62nd minute, his second goal of the tournament, and serves as a corner kick taker alongside Yasin Ayari. Viktor Gyokeres and Alexander Isak lead the Swedish attack.

Sweden scored seven goals and conceded seven across the group stage, the widest goal variance of any side reaching the knockout rounds. Yasin Ayari scored against Tunisia and has been involved in Sweden's set piece delivery throughout the tournament.

Anthony Elanga offers DFS value with corner kick volume and a recent goal against Japan, while Viktor Gyokeres and Alexander Isak provide upside as Sweden's central attacking pairing against a defense that has conceded just twice.
Mexico completed a perfect group stage with three wins and zero goals conceded, defeating South Africa 2-0, South Korea 1-0, and Czechia 3-0 to top Group A with nine points.

Julian Quinones leads Mexico with two goals in the group stage and operates as a wide attacker with license to drift centrally. Roberto Alvarado has served as Mexico's primary corner kick taker, while Raul Jimenez returns to the starting lineup after being rested against Czechia.

Mexico is the only team to complete the group stage without conceding a goal, keeping three clean sheets in three matches. Their defensive unit, anchored in midfield, has not allowed a goal in 11 consecutive matches dating back before the tournament.
Raul Jimenez headlines Mexico's DFS pool as the leading striker returning to the starting eleven, while Julian Quinones offers proven scoring output as the group stage's top Mexican goalscorer.

Ecuador advanced as one of the best third-placed teams after a dramatic 2-1 comeback win over Group E winners Germany in their final match. Gonzalo Plata scored the winning goal in the 77th minute after Nilson Angulo had equalized.

Moises Caicedo and Pedro Vite anchor Ecuador's midfield and have served as corner kick takers throughout the group stage. Ecuador conceded only twice across three group games, the third-lowest total at the tournament.

Ecuador was held to a goalless draw with Curaçao despite registering 27 shots, before producing their signature win against Germany. They scored just twice from over five expected goals in the group stage, reflecting a finishing inefficiency despite strong underlying numbers.

Gonzalo Plata offers DFS upside off his game-winning goal against Germany, with corner kick volume in tow. Moises Caicedo and Pedro Vite provide a deeper, value-priced pivot from Ecuador's defensively sound midfield.
